text:
Morgan: Heads-up — I'm sketching a follow-up to the service-auth RFC focused on background workers that cross project boundaries. Problem: we currently hand long-lived org API keys to batch workers and it's scary for blast radius.
Riya: +1. My rough preference is short-lived project-scoped tokens minted via an exchange endpoint. But token exchange adds latency and operator complexity.
Sam: Curious how this maps to RBAC: do we create per-project roles (eg `ingest.writer` + project id) or reuse global roles with project scoping? Routing and tracing depend on it.
Tess: Proposal: keep human/admin API keys org-scoped for console/ops. For services, issue ephemeral JWTs with claims {"sub":"svc:<name>", "proj":"<proj-id>", "roles":["ingest.writer"]} via a token broker. TTLs 15m-1h. Minting is authenticated by a short-lived machine cert.
Morgan: Sounds reasonable. What about offline auditability? Need a way to verify a token later without contacting broker (for logs/forensics).
Riya: We can sign tokens with a stable key and include a `kid` so auditors can verify logs. For runtime checks, caching verification results (jwks) reduces broker trips.
Sam: Edge-case: a worker legitimately touches multiple projects (cross-proj pipelines). Do we mint multi-project tokens or have actors request separate tokens per project and stitch them? Multi-project tokens increase blast radius.
Tess: Prefer many single-proj tokens and a small orchestration layer that swaps tokens per request. That keeps principle-of-least-privilege. For latency, the orchestration layer can cache tokens and reuse until TTL expiry.
sec-bot: policy-bot: Draft policy posted: https://rdrw.co/rfc/service-scope — includes token shape, `proj` claim, `aud` for routing, and revocation hints. :page_facing_up:
Morgan: Rollout concerns: a lot of infra needs updating (sidecars, SDKs, infra images). Suggest canary on internal ingestion first, fallback path to org-key for legacy jobs but heavily rate-limited.
Riya: We should add a migration metric: % of requests using ephemeral tokens, auth latency p50/p95, and failed-exchange rates. Also flag any service that requests cross-proj tokens frequently.
Tess: I'll draft the follow-up RFC with sections: threat model, token format, signing/rotation, broker auth flows, SDK examples, migration playbook. Volunteer to own. @Sam can you help with rollout automation notes?
Sam: Yep. I'll sketch the canary and fallback scripts, and a sidecar shim for token swap.
Morgan: Great — please include a short example header for usage in SDKs, e.g.:
```
Authorization: Bearer svc-eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1Ni... 
X-Rdrw-Project: proj-12345
```
Morgan: Okay, owner = Tess. Riya + Sam will review. I'll open the follow-up RFC thread later today and paste implementation tickets. :thumbsup:
